How to Prepare a Food Business Consultancy Brief

Prepare a useful food-business consultancy brief with your concept, location, budget assumptions, operating questions and expected deliverables.

Zorko Group · Business guidance · Reviewed 18 November 2026

In this guide
  1. Describe the decision you need to make
  2. Bring the available information
  3. Agree on deliverables and responsibilities
  4. Choose an evidence-based next step

Describe the decision you need to make

Explain whether you are exploring a concept, opening an outlet, improving an operation or considering expansion. A focused question helps you compare the relevance of proposed services.

Bring the available information

Gather the current menu or concept, intended customers, location options, cost estimates and any operating records. Mark missing information so assumptions can be discussed.

Agree on deliverables and responsibilities

Ask which documents, analyses, workshops or implementation support are included. Record the timeline, review points, fees, exclusions and what your own team must provide.

Choose an evidence-based next step

The first conversation should establish the problem, available evidence and information needed next. Discuss how recommendations will be assessed and who is responsible for carrying them out.

Company information and next steps

For Zorko-specific offers and current terms, refer to the official franchise page or consultancy service and confirm details directly with the team.
